items.title: Ai-Guided Wearable Technologies and Smart Healthcare Utility in Physiotherapy
items.abstract: Abstract Physiotherapy is moving from an episodic, clinic-centred model of care towards a continuous, data-informed and patient-centred model. Wearable technologies, which include inertial measurement units, surface electromyography sensors, smart textiles, photoplethysmography-based devices, pressure-sensing insoles and smart garments, now capture movement, muscle activity, physiological load and adherence data outside the clinic. When these data streams are interpreted by artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, they can be transformed into clinically meaningful information such as exercise quality, gait deviations, fall risk, fatigue, pain-related behaviour and recovery trajectories. This manuscript reviews the technological foundations of AI-guided wearables, describes their utility across musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiopulmonary, sports, geriatric and paediatric physiotherapy, and explains how they fit within a smart healthcare ecosystem built on the Internet of Medical Things, cloud analytics and tele-rehabilitation. The potential benefits include objective assessment, personalised dosing of exercise, improved adherence, remote supervision, early detection of deterioration and wider access to rehabilitation, particularly for under-served populations. The paper also examines the principal limitations: sensor validity, algorithmic bias, data privacy, regulatory uncertainty, cost, digital literacy and the risk of de-skilling. A five-layer implementation framework and a set of recommendations for clinicians, educators, researchers and policy makers are proposed. It is concluded that AI-guided wearables should be positioned as decision-support tools that extend, and never replace, the clinical reasoning and therapeutic relationship at the centre of physiotherapy practice.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Sports Performance Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract: AI is increasingly playing a significant role in sports today, and it's transforming the way athletes are evaluated, trained, and monitored. It enables coaches, sports scientists and athletes to explore vast quantities of performance data and find patterns that they might not otherwise be able to see through traditional methods. Technologies like machine learning, computer vision, wearable technology, predictive analytics, and automated video analysis are also being applied to a growing number of technical skills, physical performance, tactical movements, training workload, recovery and injury risk studies. Such technologies can deliver real-time and personalized data to coaches to create training plans based on the unique requirements of athletes and make informed decisions. AI can also aid in talent identification and performance prediction by integrating data collected from physical, physiological, biomechanical, and psychological factors. While these are advantages, there are also drawbacks to using AI in sports. Data quality, privacy, cost, technical, algorithmic bias and ethical considerations should be taken seriously. The article will explore the key applications of AI in sports performance analysis, as well as its potential benefits in enhancing athlete development and performance, and its current challenges and future prospects.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Higher Education: A Systematic Review of Opportunities, Challenges and Emerging Trends
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence AI is getting more and more involved in higher education, it is reshaping teaching, learning , assessment, academic administration, research, and even how institutions decide things. In the last few years the fast rise of generative artificial intelligence GenAI, plus intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, automated assessment, recommendation systems, and AI assisted administrative tools has opened up new possibilities for universities, yet it also brings worries like academic integrity, data privacy, algorithmic bias, digital inequality, transparency, and changing professional roles. This paper actually uses a secondary-data based systematic review, looking at research and policy sources about AI and digital transformation in higher education. The review brings together outcomes from academic studies, other systematic reviews, and international policy frameworks, sort of to map out the main uses, opportunities, obstacles, and the kind of emerging trends that are starting to show up. What the literature suggests is that AI in education is not only about making content. It also includes adaptive learning, personalized tutoring, intelligent assessment, profiling and prediction, and support for institutional management. At the same time, good adoption does not just happen, it needs institutional policies, AI literacy, ethical safety nets, teacher professional development, careful responsible assessment approaches, and a human centered way of putting things into practice. A number of recent international frameworks stress human agency, ethics, AI competencies, and responsible usage, so there is a clear direction there. Overall the review shows that AI is best understood as augmentation tech with AI to help educators and learners not to flip a switch and replace the educational roles that already exist. items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Transformations in the Labour Market
items.abstract: Abstract One of the most transformative technologies of the twenty first century is Artificial Intelligence (AI) which has had a great impact on the global labour market. The adoption of AI technologies, including machine learning, robotics, natural language processing, and automation systems, into various sectors has reshaped employment landscape, productivity dynamics, and job demands in developed and developing countries. This research paper will analyze the effects of AI on the global labour market, including changes in job trends, job displacement, skill transformation, productivity gains, wage inequality, and labour market polarization. The study also explores sector-specific shifts in manufacturing, healthcare, financial services, retail, logistics, education and information technology. The method of the research is mixed (qualitative and quantitative) and the data used is secondary data obtained from international organizations namely International Labour Organization (ILO), World Economic Forum (WEF), Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank. 2018 - 2025 data is analyzed to gain insight into the evolving job market as AI impacts it. The study highlights the positive impact of AI on productivity, efficiency, and economic growth, but also points to the potential challenges posed by AI such as job displacement and technological unemployment, the increasing income gap, and skill mismatches. The results show that only jobs with repetitive or routine tasks are at risk of being automated while jobs that need creativity, emotional intelligence, and high-level analytical skills are still increasing. Additionally, the paper discusses the new job roles in data science, AI engineering, cyber security, digital marketing, and the human-machine interaction. Digital infrastructure, technological readiness and the lack of training of the workforce are all challenges that developing countries have to overcome. Developed economies, on the other hand, are more likely to do so via innovation ecosystems and skill development programs. The study makes an important point about the importance of inclusive labour market transitions for the role of the governments, educational institutions, multinational corporations and international organisations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Climate Change Prediction
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change presents a growing danger to ecosystems, infrastructure, and human safety, heightening the need for prediction systems that are both precise and rapid enough to facilitate prompt decision-making. Artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning, has arisen as a revolutionary enhancement to conventional physics-based numerical models. This manuscript examines the application of AI methodologies, such as graph neural networks, transformers, Fourier neural operators, and ensemble deep-learning frameworks, throughout the climate-prediction continuum, encompassing short-term weather forecasting to multi-decadal climate model simulation, sea-level forecasting, and greenhouse gas emission estimation. We encapsulate notable systems documented in contemporary literature, examine the computational and scientific benefits that AI presents in comparison to traditional numerical weather prediction (NWP), and delineate the key obstacles, such as data insufficiency, physical coherence, interpretability, and energy expenditure, that need resolution prior to the reliable implementation of AI-driven climate forecasting at an operational level. We finish with guidance on hybrid physics-AI modelling as a means to get dependable, practical climate insights.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Institutional Accreditation in India: A Framework for NAAC's Data-Driven Quality Assurance
items.abstract: Abstract For nearly three decades, the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) has been India's main mechanism for assuring quality in higher education. Its traditional model — built around a self-reported Self-Study Report, a data validation stage, and an on-site peer-team visit ending in a letter grade — has come under increasing strain. Critics point to slow turnaround, difficulty in standardizing judgments across assessor teams, and the challenge of scaling the process to the thousands of institutions India now wishes to bring under formal quality review. In February 2025, NAAC announced a major reform: a binary accreditation outcome, an optional five-level Maturity-Based Graded Level (MBGL) scale for institutions seeking continuous improvement, a unified national data platform, and the beginnings of an AI-assisted evaluation engine to reduce the burden of manual verification. This paper builds on that reform and proposes, in concrete technical terms, what such an AI-assisted engine could look like. We outline a system that can read and structure Self-Study Reports, cross-check institutional claims against government data sources such as UGC, AICTE, AISHE and NIRF, benchmark institutions against their peers, and present the results to human assessors without replacing their judgment. The discussion is grounded in India's higher-education context: wide variation in digital readiness across institutions, obligations under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the well-known risk that metric-driven systems can encourage institutions to "write to the metric" rather than improve underlying quality. We conclude with a phased pilot study to test the framework before any wider rollout.

items.title: Cognitive Reserve Depletion and Learning Autonomy Recovery in Generative Artificial Intelligence Dependent Educational Environments
items.abstract: This study examines how generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) dependence relates to cognitive reserve depletion and learning autonomy among university students. Using a quasi-experimental design, the study involved 120 students from two universities in Padang, Indonesia, divided equally into intervention and control groups. Data were analyzed using linear regression and ANCOVA following a four-week learning autonomy recovery program. The statistical estimates showed a positive relationship between AI dependence and cognitive reserve depletion (B = 0.698, p < 0.001), while cognitive reserve depletion was negatively associated with learning autonomy (B = −0.482, p < 0.001). The intervention showed a positive adjusted effect (B = 0.334, p < 0.001), highlighting the importance of developing independent learning practices alongside AI use.

items.title: Continuous Auditing: AI systems that monitor transactions in real time
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the auditing profession by enabling continuous auditing systems capable of monitoring financial transactions in real time. Unlike traditional auditing methods, which rely on periodic reviews, AI-driven continuous auditing facilitates automated transaction analysis, anomaly detection, fraud prevention, and timely risk assessment. This study examines the role of AI in enhancing the effectiveness of continuous auditing by evaluating its impact on audit efficiency, fraud detection, internal controls, and organizational decision-making. A descriptive research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 100 respondents, including auditors, accountants, finance professionals, and postgraduate students through a structured questionnaire. Secondary data were gathered from scholarly journals, books, industry reports, and professional publications. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square analysis, Pearson correlation, and regression analysis. The findings reveal a significant association between AI awareness and perceptions of audit efficiency (χ² = 23.67, p < 0.05). Further, a strong positive relationship exists between AI adoption and continuous auditing effectiveness (r = 0.784), with AI adoption explaining 61.5% of the variation in auditing effectiveness (R² = 0.615). The study concludes that AI-powered continuous auditing significantly improves the accuracy, speed, and reliability of financial transaction monitoring while strengthening fraud detection and internal controls. Despite challenges relating to implementation costs, data security, and technical expertise, AI offers substantial opportunities to enhance audit quality and support sound financial governance in the digital era.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Systems: A Critical Review of Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain Approaches for Trading, Fraud Detection, and Price Prediction
items.abstract: Cryptocurrency has become an important part of the digital financial ecosystem, offering new opportunities while also introducing challenges related to trading, price prediction, fraud detection, and financial security. This paper presents a critical review of how Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, and Blockchain technologies are being applied to address these challenges. It examines 15 selected IEEE research papers covering various approaches, including deep learning-based price prediction, reinforcement learning for automated trading, sentiment analysis, transaction network analysis, and blockchain-based fraud detection. The review compares the methods, datasets, reported results, and limitations of these studies, while highlighting important concerns such as prediction accuracy, trading profitability, fraudulent transaction identification, data privacy, explainability, and the energy consumption of cryptocurrency mining. It also discusses the strengths and weaknesses of existing approaches and identifies areas that require further research. Overall, this paper aims to provide students, researchers, and readers with a clear understanding of current developments, practical challenges, and future research opportunities in applying AI and Blockchain technologies to cryptocurrency systems.

items.abstract: Abstract The study titled “Current Sustainability Science, Environment and Artificial Intelligence: Digital Role in Human Well-being” examines the growing role of science, digital technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) in promoting sustainable development and improving human well-being. It explores the applications of AI and digital tools in education, healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, industry, business, transportation, public services, and economic development. The study employs survey and descriptive observation methods, drawing on online information, research articles, reference books, and other sources. It highlights how AI can support informed decision-making, improve access to information, enhance agricultural productivity, assist medical diagnosis, monitor environmental changes, and facilitate services for persons with disabilities. However, the study also emphasizes the limitations and potential risks associated with excessive or irresponsible use of digital technologies. It argues that artificial intelligence should complement, rather than replace, human intelligence and decision-making. The effective use of these technologies requires transparency, safety, ethical responsibility, and inclusiveness. The study concludes that the constructive and responsible integration of science, digital technology, and AI can contribute significantly to sustainable development, environmental protection, social welfare, and the well-being of present and future generations.

items.title: Deforestation & Land-Use Change: Artificial Intelligence Approaches for Detection, Attribution, and Predictive Monitoring Of Global Forest Loss
items.abstract: Abstract Deforestation and land-use change remain among the most consequential drivers of biodiversity loss, carbon emissions, and hydrological disruption worldwide. Traditional monitoring approaches, which rely on periodic satellite surveys and manual interpretation, are often too slow to support timely conservation intervention. This article reviews the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) including machine learning, deep learning, and multi-modal data fusion to the detection, attribution, and prediction of deforestation. We synthesize current methodologies spanning random forests, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), U-Net segmentation, and vision transformers, applied to optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery. Comparative performance data, regional case studies, and driver-attribution frameworks are presented alongside supporting tables and infographics. The review finds that fusion models combining optical and radar data currently achieve the highest reported accuracy (>96%) and that explainable AI (XAI) integration remains an underexplored but increasingly critical requirement for policy adoption. We conclude with a discussion of current limitations including data scarcity in the Global South, cloud interference, and selective-logging detection and propose directions for future research, including transfer learning for low-resource regions and carbon-stock-linked monitoring pipelines.

items.abstract: Abstract Digital innovation is transforming agriculture from conventional production systems into intelligent, data-driven, connected, and increasingly autonomous ecosystems. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), robotics, cloud computing, blockchain, digital twins, big data analytics, and mobile-based agricultural services is enabling farmers to make timely and informed decisions throughout the agricultural value chain. Digital technologies support precision crop management, soil and crop monitoring, irrigation optimization, pest and disease detection, weather forecasting, farm mechanization, supply-chain management, market access, and post-harvest management. These innovations can improve resource-use efficiency, productivity, profitability, climate resilience, and sustainability. However, limited digital infrastructure, high initial investment, lack of technical skills, fragmented data ecosystems, cybersecurity risks, interoperability challenges, and unequal access to technology remain significant barriers, particularly for smallholder farmers. This review examines the evolution and major dimensions of digital innovation in agriculture, discusses emerging technologies and their applications, evaluates opportunities and challenges, and presents future directions toward Agriculture 4.0 and Agriculture 5.0. The paper emphasizes the need for farmer-centric, affordable, interoperable, secure, and inclusive digital ecosystems to ensure that technological innovation contributes effectively to sustainable agricultural development.

items.title: Digital Transformation and Organizational Performance: An Empirical Study of Selected Indian Organizations
items.abstract: Abstract Digital transformation has emerged as an important strategic priority for organizations seeking to improve operational efficiency, innovation, customer experience and overall organizational performance. The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data analytics, automation and digital platforms has significantly changed the way organizations operate and make managerial decisions. This study examines the relationship between digital transformation and organizational performance in selected Indian organizations. The study focuses on major dimensions of digital transformation, including digital technology adoption, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and automation, data analytics, digital platforms, and digital capabilities of employees. Organizational performance is examined in terms of operational efficiency, employee productivity, innovation, customer satisfaction and business performance. The study adopts a quantitative research design and proposes the collection of primary data through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation and regression analysis are proposed for testing the relationship between digital transformation and organizational performance. The study is expected to provide useful insights for managers and organizations regarding the role of digital technologies in improving organizational outcomes.

items.title: Digital-Age Ethics for Elementary Teachers: Challenges and Strategies for Professional Integrity
items.abstract: Digital transformation has expanded elementary teachers’ work into learning platforms, social media, messaging applications, data systems, and generative artificial intelligence. These tools support collaboration and instructional improvement but raise ethical concerns about professional boundaries, children’s privacy and safety, information integrity, copyright, equity, and accountability. This article synthesizes the ethical challenges faced by elementary school teachers in digital environments and identifies strategies for maintaining professional integrity while prioritizing children’s best interests. A narrative literature review was conducted through exploratory searches of scholarly articles, academic books, international frameworks, policy documents, and Indonesian legislation, prioritizing publications from 2020 to 2026 alongside foundational theories. The thematic synthesis identifies risks involving blurred personal and professional boundaries, children’s data governance, unsafe online communication, unverified digital and AI-generated content, and unequal access to technology. It proposes a Five-Dimension Framework of Teachers’ Digital Integrity comprising pedagogical, relational, information-and-data, epistemic, and civic-professional integrity. Recommendations are directed to teachers, schools, teacher education programs, families, and professional associations. The framework is a conceptual synthesis, not a validated instrument, and requires empirical testing in Indonesian elementary schools

items.title: Drawbacks and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in the Medical Field
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an important technology in modern healthcare. It is being used for medical image analysis, disease prediction, clinical decision support, drug discovery, patient monitoring, and administrative activities. AI can improve the speed and efficiency of healthcare, but its use also introduces significant risks. This paper examines the major drawbacks of AI in the medical field, including algorithmic bias, inaccurate predictions, lack of explainability, privacy and security risks, high implementation costs, overdependence on automated systems, accountability problems, and lack of quality training data, ethical concerns, and unequal access to AI-based healthcare. The World Health Organization (WHO) has specifically emphasized the importance of safety, transparency, human autonomy, accountability, equity, and privacy when implementing AI in healthcare. The paper also discusses possible solutions and future research directions for developing safe, reliable, and responsible medical AI.

items.title: Edge AI for Energy-Efficient Smart IoT Systems: A Sustainable Computing Approach
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) is transforming Internet of Things (IoT) systems by enabling data-driven decisions close to the point where data are generated. However, conventional cloud-centric architectures can introduce communication overhead, latency, privacy concerns, and additional energy costs. This paper examines Edge AI as a sustainable computing approach for energy-efficient smart IoT systems, with particular relevance to the development priorities associated with Viksit Bharat 2047. The study follows a descriptive and analytical approach based on research literature concerning TinyML, on-device machine learning, Edge AI, and energy-aware IoT. It proposes an architecture consisting of sensing, local inference, edge coordination, selective cloud processing, and energy-aware orchestration. The paper further identifies measurable parameters including accuracy, inference latency, energy per inference, communication volume, memory footprint, and reliability for evaluating sustainable AIoT systems. The objective is not to claim unverified experimental results, but to establish a practical research framework that can subsequently be tested on resource-constrained edge hardware. The study indicates that sustainable AIoT should be evaluated not only through predictive performance but also through the computational, communication, and energy resources required to deliver each intelligent decision.

items.title: Exploring the integration of artificial intelligence into residency education curriculum: qualitative interviews
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in medical practice, the importance of integrating AI curricula into postgraduate medical education (PGME) grows. While frameworks outlining necessary AI competencies for physicians exist, there is little consensus on how these competencies can be effectively implemented at the PGME level. Understanding the barriers and enablers to AI curricular integration is essential in preparing residents for an AI-enabled healthcare system. This study aims to explore expert perspectives on the ethical, institutional, and process-related challenges of integrating AI into PGME curriculum. Methods We conducted a qualitative study using an interpretive descriptive approach. Twelve physicians involved in AI and medical education across North America participated in semi-structured virtual interviews. Participants were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling. Interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed. Interview transcripts were analyzed using applied thematic analysis, with independent dual coding and consensus-based refinement of a structured codebook. Reflexive memos and analytic discussions supported rigor. Results Twelve interviews were completed; recruitment concluded at a pragmatic stopping point once successive interviews were judged to be converging on a consistent set of issues. Five major themes emerged: (1) the need for curricular agility in the face of rapid AI evolution, (2) gaps in faculty expertise, (3) limited institutional and regulatory readiness, (4) the role of nationally endorsed curricular standards, and (5) cultural resistance related to professional identity and responsibility. Participants emphasized prioritizing modular competencies, adopting co-learning models to address faculty limitations, and seeking clearer guidance from governing bodies. Conclusion Our findings offer practical guidance for educators on integrating AI into PGME curriculum. Building agile content, investing in multidisciplinary faculty development, fostering institutional and regulatory readiness, establishing national standards, and addressing cultural shifts can help PGME programs responsibly deploy AI curricula. In doing so, programs can position their graduates as reflective, ethical, and advanced clinicians capable of safely employing AI to improve patient care.

items.title: Financial Inclusion and Institutional Resilience in AI-Driven Islamic Finance: A Contract-Based Risk Governance Framework
items.abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Islamic finance has complicated the allocation of responsibility when financing decisions depend on automated assessments. This study develops a conceptual governance framework by reconstructing the complementary functions of Kafalah, Wakalah, and rahn. Using a qualitative doctrinal-comparative approach, it examines the contracts individually and through three pairwise relationships, then maps their functions to AI-related risks and institutional controls. The analysis identifies Kafalah–rahn as a mechanism for coordinating guarantees and collateral, Kafalah–Wakalah for linking guarantee obligations with accountable delegation, and Wakalah–rahn for governing delegated collateral activities. These relationships inform a five-layer architecture covering contractual authority, contingent risk allocation, collateral risk mitigation, technological governance, and maqāṣid al-sharīʿah-based evaluation. An illustrative financing scenario shows how model validation, human oversight, decision traceability, and proportionate safeguards may operate together. The framework distinguishes responsible financial access from institutional resilience without assuming that either outcome follows automatically. Its contribution is conceptual, and practical effectiveness requires subsequent expert and institutional assessment.

items.title: From Prompt to Polygon: Evaluating End-to-End Human–AI Workflows for Web-Based Generative 3D Authoring
items.abstract: Prompt- and image-driven 3D generation can lower the interaction barrier to digital asset creation, yet model-level advances do not establish whether non-specialists can operate a complete authoring workflow. This study designed and evaluated a web-based human–AI prototype integrating a React interface, FastAPI services, ComfyUI workflow orchestration, asynchronous job processing, persistent asset storage, and browser-based 3D visualization. We implemented four modes: Text-to-3D, Text-to-3D with ControlNet, Single Image-to-3D, and Multi Image-to-3D. Evaluation combined 14 requirement-derived black-box scenarios, cross-viewer GLB compatibility checks in three viewing environments, 35 completed generation jobs, task-based observation with seven participants completing 84 task executions, System Usability Scale (SUS) responses from a separate group of 12 students, and one expert assessment of implementation and output quality. All 14 functional scenarios produced the expected outcomes, and the tested GLB outputs opened in the integrated viewer, Blender, and 3dviewer.net. Mean server-side turnaround was 66.15 s; an exploratory Kruskal–Wallis test indicated differences among the observed workload distributions (H(3) = 10.52, p = .015, ε² = .243), but did not support causal or pairwise speed claims. All observed tasks were eventually completed, but only 61 of 84 executions (72.62%) were independent; Tasks 5 (enter Studio) and 10 (find the generated model in My Projects) each required assistance for five of seven participants. Mean SUS was 81.67 (SD = 9.25; 95% CI [75.79, 87.55]), while generated-model quality received a diagnostic expert score of 3.50/5. The study contributes an end-to-end human–AI authoring architecture and a multidimensional evaluation logic that separates functional conformance, deployment turnaround, cross-viewer compatibility, observed interaction, perceived usability, and output quality. Findings support the feasibility of accessible web-based generative 3D authoring while identifying discoverability and geometric-quality constraints.

items.title: Future directions on integrated wildlife monitoring based on non-invasive approaches in Europe
items.abstract: Abstract The growing trend of emerging diseases at the wildlife-livestock-human interface underscores the need to establish integrated surveillance strategies within a One Health framework. In Europe, Integrated Wildlife Monitoring (IWM) tends to focus on specific pathogens, often with limited spatial and temporal scope. In this perspectives article, we address some of the most recent technological advances that could strengthen future IWM programs, with special emphasis on non-invasive approaches for monitoring wildlife populations and pathogen communities. We analyse the potential complementarity of different monitoring tools, such as camera traps, unmanned aerial vehicles, acoustic recording, and especially the detection of environmental nucleic acids (ENAD) using next-generation sequencing techniques, for the simultaneous characterization of pathogen and host communities. Despite the potential of molecular tools for large-scale monitoring, the lack of methodological standardization, the limited capacity to obtain quantitative information (e.g. population abundance or pathogen prevalence), and the difficulty of inferring the epidemiological significance of findings (e.g. whether molecular detection indicates viable pathogen) remain key challenges that limit their application. Finally, we argue that integrating these technologies with artificial intelligence (AI) represents a promising approach for managing large, heterogeneous datasets and developing proactive early warning systems. Moving toward the implementation of standardized and harmonized strategies that integrate ecological and epidemiological information should be a priority in European health surveillance frameworks. Strengthening coordination among surveillance systems by incorporating multi-source, AI-supported approaches will be key to improving early detection capacity and supporting evidence-based decision-making in addressing the global emergence of diseases.

items.title: Generative AI in Elementary Teacher Education: Opportunities, Risks, and Professional Ethics
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may influence how prospective elementary school teachers design, implement, and evaluate learning. It can support idea generation, lesson planning, differentiated activities, assessment rubrics, and reflective practice. However, fluent outputs are not necessarily accurate, developmentally appropriate, unbiased, or aligned with the curriculum and local sociocultural contexts. This article synthesizes the pedagogical opportunities, risks, and professional-ethical implications of GenAI use in Indonesian elementary teacher education and proposes directions for responsible integration. The study employs a narrative literature review based on exploratory searches of SciSpace, journal-publisher websites, academic sources, UNESCO publications, and Indonesian education-policy documents. The core literature covers 2020–2026, complemented by relevant foundational theory. The thematic synthesis identifies potential benefits for lesson planning and differentiation, alongside risks involving hallucinations, bias, developmental inappropriateness, privacy, copyright, unequal access, and cognitive overdependence. Responsible use requires AI literacy beyond prompt writing, including critical evaluation, ethical judgment, transparency, and accountability. The article proposes the KONTEKS framework as a guide for contextualizing, verifying, adapting, and taking responsibility for GenAI outputs. As a narrative review, it does not claim exhaustive systematic coverage or quantitative effect estimates; its recommendations require empirical testing in Indonesian elementary teacher education programs

items.title: GeoAI for Sustainable Futures: Integrating Artificial Intelligence, Earth Observation and GIS for Environmental Resilience
items.abstract: Abstract Geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI), the integration of artificial intelligence with Earth Observation (EO) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS), is reshaping how environmental resilience is monitored and managed. This paper reviews GeoAI as both a technical practice and a geographical problem, arguing that its value for resilience planning depends on respecting the spatial properties — dependence, heterogeneity and scale — that distinguish geographic data from ordinary tabular data. The paper synthesises published evidence across four resilience-relevant domains: land use/land cover (LULC) change detection, drought risk assessment, landslide hazard zonation and groundwater potential mapping and situates this evidence within the Deccan Plateau and Western Ghats margin of Maharashtra, a terrain that compresses escarpment landslide risk, valley land-use change and rain-shadow drought within a single administrative region. The review finds consistent but bounded accuracy gains from machine-learning methods over conventional GIS overlay, with the largest gains reported where training and validation data are collected locally rather than transferred from elsewhere. The paper closes with a phased adoption roadmap for a teaching-and-research college operating in this terrain, arguing that institutional investment in ground-truth data collection should precede investment in more elaborate models.

items.title: Green Intelligence 5.0: Designing a Net-Positive Digital Future through Artificial Intelligence, Environmental Sustainability, and Human Well-being
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a general-purpose layer across education, healthcare, agriculture, energy, manufacturing and governance. It can strengthen climate-risk mapping, renewable-energy forecasting, precision irrigation, biodiversity monitoring, waste sorting and early-warning systems. Yet AI is not immaterial: computation depends on electricity, cooling, water, hardware, minerals, networks and labour, while rapid equipment turnover adds to electronic waste. This paper asks how AI can be designed so that its verified benefits for people and the planet outweigh its lifecycle burdens. Using an integrative evidence-synthesis and conceptual framework approach, the paper proposes Green Intelligence 5.0, a six-pillar architecture integrating ecological responsibility, responsible AI, circular infrastructure, inclusion, human well-being and accountable governance. Three practical contributions are introduced: the GROW-AI operating model, a 30-point Green Intelligence Scorecard, and a Net-Positive-by-Design decision rule. Recent global indicators illustrate the scale of the challenge: the International Energy Agency estimated data-centre electricity use at about 415 TWh in 2024 and projects approximately 945 TWh by 2030 in its base case; the Global E-waste Monitor reported 62 billion kg of e-waste in 2022, with 22.3% documented as formally collected and recycled. These figures are presented as sourced contextual indicators, not as original measurements by the authors. The framework is mapped to SDGs 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16, with an India-focused proposition: “AI for All, Green by Design.” The paper concludes that digital progress should be assessed by net human and planetary value—not computational scale alone.

items.title: History of Indian Environment and the Role of Artificial Intelligence: An Analytical Study of Water Management, Climate Change, and Digital History Research
items.abstract: Abstract The development of Indian civilization is the story of the inter-relationship between water, land, forests, agriculture and human society. The town planning and drainage system of the Indus Valley Civilisation, ancient knowledge of water in India, ponds-wells-dams-canals, water planning by Malik Ambar, water resources and forts during the Maratha rule and the shifting control during the colonial period are subjects that can be explored under the umbrella of environmental history. Issues such as climate change, dwindling ground water resources, erratic rainfall, urbanisation and water contamination are becoming more complex today. Consequently, the linkage between historical knowledge and digital tool and AI becomes critical. The primary goal of this study is to look at the traditional system of water management in Indian environmental history, understand the potential of AI, GIS, satellite imagery, OCR and big data analysis in the field of digital history research and explore the correlation between historical environmental knowledge and sustainable development. Historical texts, inscriptions, maps, archaeological reports, digital archives, research articles, and current water resources information have been used in the study analytically.

items.title: Human Values in the Digital Era
items.abstract: Abstract The digital era has transformed communication, education, work, commerce, governance and social interaction. Artificial intelligence, social media, smartphones, digital platforms, cloud services and data-driven systems have created unprecedented opportunities for access to knowledge and participation. At the same time, digital life has intensified ethical questions concerning privacy, truth, dignity, empathy, responsibility, justice, equality, autonomy and human well-being. This conceptual research paper examines the significance of human values in the digital era and explores how technological progress can be guided by a human-centred ethical framework. The paper is based on a qualitative conceptual review of selected books and educational and policy-oriented literature related to human values, technology, digital citizenship, ethics and education. The analysis indicates that technology itself is neither automatically beneficial nor harmful; its social consequences depend substantially on the values embedded in its design, use and governance. The paper identifies respect, responsibility, honesty, empathy, compassion, justice, privacy, digital self-discipline, critical thinking and sustainability as important values for responsible digital life. It further argues that educational institutions have a central role in developing value-based digital citizenship by integrating ethical reasoning, media literacy, information literacy, cyber safety and reflective use of technology. A balanced approach is required in which innovation is encouraged while human dignity and social responsibility remain at the centre. The paper concludes that the future of digital society should be evaluated not only by speed, efficiency and intelligence, but also by whether technology strengthens human relationships, democratic participation, inclusion and holistic well-being.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Modules into Traditional Master of Business Administration Core Curricula to Enhance Modern Business Education and Leadership Readiness
items.abstract: Abstract: The paradigm of modern commerce has shifted irreversibly, driven by the exponential proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and disruptive technological innovations. Traditional Master of Business Administration (MBA) programs, historically anchored in static case methodologies and compartmentalized functional silos (e.g., finance, marketing, operations, and strategic management), face mounting pressure to bridge the gap between legacy pedagogy and contemporary industry demands. This paper examines the imperative for seamlessly embedding AI and innovation modules into core MBA curricula. By analyzing the systemic transition of AI from an experimental peripheral tool to an enterprise-wide operational architecture, this study outlines a comprehensive framework for cultivating digitally fluent, ethically grounded, and change-ready business leaders. We propose a holistic curriculum redesign that transcends isolated technical electives, infusing data literacy, algorithmic decision-making, prompt engineering, and human-centric innovation management directly into core business courses. Furthermore, the paper addresses institutional barriers, faculty readiness, and the delicate equilibrium between technical proficiency and foundational emotional intelligence. Ultimately, this research posits that modernizing graduate business education through structured AI and innovation integration is essential for safeguarding the societal relevance, practical efficacy, and leadership readiness of future executives.

items.title: Internet of Things (IoT): Applications, Benefits, Challenges and Future Scope
items.abstract: Abstract The Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly developing technology that enables physical objects to connect to the internet and exchange data with other devices and systems. These objects may include household appliances, vehicles, industrial machines, medical equipment, agricultural systems, and smart-city infrastructure. IoT combines sensors, communication networks, cloud computing, data analytics, and artificial intelligence to collect and process information and support intelligent decision-making. This research paper examines the concept and architecture of IoT, its major technologies, applications, advantages, challenges, security concerns, and future scope. The paper concludes that IoT has significant potential to improve efficiency, automation, safety, and quality of life across various sectors, although privacy, cyber security interoperability, and scalability remain important challenges.

items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides opportunities to support the learning process, but it also presents challenges related to ethics, data security, academic integrity, and responsible use of digital technology. This community service activity aimed to improve AI literacy among students and parents by strengthening their understanding of safe, ethical, and responsible AI use. The activity was conducted at SDN 25 Madello over a two-month period, involving students and parents as participants. The method employed an educational-participatory approach through material delivery, discussions, practical activities, case studies, and evaluation. The materials covered an introduction to AI, the use of AI in learning, AI ethics, academic integrity, personal data protection and security, and legal awareness in the digital environment. The activity was conducted through collaboration among the fields of Education, Constitutional Law, and Islamic Family Law. The results indicated an improvement in participants’ understanding of the benefits and risks of AI use, as well as the importance of verifying information, protecting personal data, and using AI responsibly. The activity also demonstrated the importance of parental involvement in supporting children’s AI use at home. Cross-disciplinary collaboration provided a comprehensive approach to developing a generation that is aware, critical, and responsible in utilizing AI.

items.title: Multi Eye disease Detection in fundus images: A Structured Review
items.abstract: Abstract Deep learning (DL) has rapidly advanced automated analysis of retinal fundus images, enabling scalable screening and grading of multiple sight-threatening conditions. This review synthesizes evidence on DL methods for diabetic retinopathy (DR), glaucoma, diabetic macular edema (DME), retinal vessel tortuosity, age-related macular degeneration (ARMD/AMD), macular fibrosis, and fundus neoplasms. We examine preprocessing pipelines, model architectures (CNNs, transformers, hybrids), datasets, evaluation metrics, and clinical performance, drawing on recent systematic reviews, multi-disease benchmarks, and regulator-approved system audits. Findings indicate high accuracy for DR and AMD classification (often >0.90 AUROC/sensitivity), promising but more variable results for glaucoma and DME from fundus alone, and emerging capability for tortuosity quantification and tumor triage. Key challenges include domain shift, data quality/gradability, class imbalance for rare entities (fibrosis, neoplasms), and the need for explainability and external validation. We conclude with recommendations for robust, clinically deployable pipelines and future research directions in multimodal integration and foundation models.

items.title: Philosophy, Ethics and Artificial Intelligence a Human-Centred Framework for Responsible Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has developed from a specialised area of computer science into a general-purpose technology that increasingly influences education, healthcare, finance, employment, communication, governance and everyday decision-making. This expansion makes AI not only a technological subject but also a philosophical and ethical concern. This conceptual research paper examines the relationship between philosophy, ethics and artificial intelligence from a human-centred perspective. It analyses the ethical significance of human dignity, autonomy, privacy, justice, fairness, transparency, accountability, responsibility and sustainability. The study uses qualitative conceptual analysis of philosophical literature, AI ethics scholarship and major institutional frameworks. Particular attention is given to deontological ethics, consequentialism, virtue ethics and selected Indian ethical ideas. The paper further examines algorithmic bias, surveillance, opacity, manipulation, employment transformation, education, environmental impact and the problem of assigning responsibility for AI-mediated decisions. Contemporary frameworks of UNESCO, OECD, NIST and NITI Aayog are examined as important attempts to translate ethical principles into governance and risk-management practices. The analysis indicates that responsible AI cannot be achieved by technical safeguards alone. Ethical reasoning needs to be integrated across the complete AI lifecycle, from problem formulation and data selection to design, testing, deployment, monitoring and retirement. A human-centred framework is proposed around eight principles: human dignity, human agency, non-maleficence, justice and inclusion, privacy, explainability and contestability, accountability, and sustainability. The paper concludes that the fundamental question for the AI era is not merely what machines can do, but what human purposes, values and limits should guide their development and use.

items.title: Precision Agriculture Using AI for Crop Yield Prediction and Disease Detection: A Comprehensive Review of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches for Sustainable, Data-Driven Farming
items.abstract: Abstract Precision agriculture amalgamates artificial intelligence (AI) with field-level sensors to enhance agricultural yield while reducing resource use. This article offers an extensive examination of the application of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methodologies to two essential functions: forecasting crop production based on environmental and soil information, and identifying plant diseases using leaf images. We investigate the historical evolution of the discipline, outline prevalent data sources and preprocessing methodologies, evaluate the reported efficacy of prominent model families across various benchmark analyses, showcase representative case-study workflows, and assess the resource and economic implications of AI-assisted agriculture. We provide a deeper examination of regional deployment trends, delineate the practical and technological obstacles hindering large-scale implementation, and suggest prospective research avenues such as federated learning, edge deployment, and interpretable AI. The evaluation aims to function as a comprehensive resource for scholars and professionals exploring this swiftly advancing domain.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) structures rely on large amounts of private records for training and deployment. This creates privacy concerns that common fact safety systems now would not have been designed to handle, along with opaque statistical series, net scraping without meaningful consent, inferences about sensitive features, leakage of training statistics from models, surveillance, and automated decision making. The rapid development of generative AI has heightened those concerns, as fashions that are proficient on internet-scale data currently are used by tens of millions of those who mechanically embed private records into them. It assesses the main legal frameworks, particularly the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the EU AI Act, and India’s Digital Personal Information Protection Act, 2023, and identifies gaps in how they handle inferred facts, educated fashions, and enforcement of erasure rights. It also considers regulatory enforcement enjoy, consisting of actions against Clearview AI and ChatGPT, to show how current regulation is applied to AI in practice. Finally, it evaluates technical security measures consisting of differential privacy and connected knowing, along with organizational measures consisting of privacy-by-design, impact assessments, and independent audits. The paper argues that effective security requires the implementation of legal responsibilities mixed with privacy-preserving engineering, instead of either on my own, and that responsibility should be shifted upstream to people who design, train, and deploy AI systems. It concludes with suggestions for regulators, with special reference to the Indian context.

items.title: Psychologically Friendly Schools: The Impact of School Well-Being on Islamic Primary School Student Engagement
items.abstract: A psychologically friendly school environment is related to school well-being and student involvement in learning. Although these two aspects have been extensively researched, empirical evidence in the context of Islamic primary schools in Indonesia still needs to be expanded. This study aims to describe school welfare and student involvement and analyze the relationship between the two in grades IV–VI. The study uses a quantitative approach with an ex post facto correlational design. A total of 57 students were selected through purposive sampling techniques. Data were collected using a Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics, normality tests, linearity tests, and simple linear regression. The results showed that school well-being and student involvement were in the moderate category. There was a positive and significant relationship between the two variables (Y = 7.756 + 0.484X; t = 4.744; p < 0.001; R = 0.539). A value of R² = 0.290 indicates that school well-being explains 29% of the variation in student engagement. These findings enrich the empirical evidence in the context of Islamic primary education and emphasize the importance of strengthening positive relationships between students and designing learning that encourages cognitive engagement. The cross-sectional design does not allow for the drawing of cause-and-effect conclusions.

items.title: Public Health and Digital Technology: Opportunities, Challenges and A District-Level Framework for Parbhani, Maharashtra
items.abstract: Abstract Digital technology has become an important component of contemporary public-health systems. Telemedicine, mobile health applications, electronic health records, digital identity, health information systems, remote monitoring, artificial intelligence and data analytics can support prevention, early detection, referral, continuity of care and population-level surveillance. India has developed a substantial digital-health ecosystem, including the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and eSanjeevani. WHO describes digital health as an area with major potential to improve access, decision-making and health-system performance, while also emphasizing equity, interoperability and responsible implementation. [1–5] This paper examines the relationship between public health and digital technology with special reference to Parbhani district of Maharashtra. It uses a narrative review and policy-analysis approach based on WHO documents, Government of India sources, Census material and recent peer-reviewed literature. The paper discusses potential applications in primary healthcare, maternal and child health, nutrition, noncommunicable disease management, infectious-disease surveillance, health education and referral services. Particular attention is given to the rural–urban digital divide, digital literacy, connectivity, privacy, cybersecurity, interoperability and workforce readiness. A district-level framework is proposed to connect community-level workers with digital registration, teleconsultation, electronic records and public-health analytics. The paper argues that technology should complement rather than replace human-centred public-health services. For Parbhani, a phased approach combining infrastructure, training, assisted digital access, data governance and local evaluation can support more equitable digital health development.

items.title: Responsible Management of Artificial Intelligence in Education: Balancing Innovation, Ethics, and Student Well-Being
items.abstract: Abstract Integration of AI in the educational system is rapidly changing the face of education by offering new possibilities of personalized learning and efficient management at the same time creating serious issues related to student autonomy, data security, and psychology. The paper suggests a holistic framework for the management of AI in education by using recommendations for the responsible use of AI in various spheres developed by international organizations like UNESCO together with recent findings about the psychological state of students. We suggest that successful integration of AI into educational practices should be based on a transition from technology-based management of AI to human-based one where student well-being becomes one of the major ethical considerations.

items.title: Robust NLP for Social Good: Transformer-Based Classification of Noisy Disaster-Related Social Media Messages
items.abstract: Abstract In the wake of terrible occurrences, social media has become the preferred source for real-time information. Social media has become a significant instrument for victims of catastrophes to express their needs, document incidents, request support and share information related to their situation. However, automated analysis may be fairly difficult in the case of casual, abbreviated, grammatically inconsistent, spelling-variant and other textual noisy communications. Artificial intelligence may be used to this data to enhance the response to catastrophes provided by technology and the well-being of humans and help in the improved detection and organization of communications related to disasters. The current research is a study on the feasibility of the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) based on transformers to classify the social media postings about the tragedy with background noise. A social media dataset related to catastrophes is pre-processed adequately to develop classification models. For the comparison of the performance of the handling of textual content on catastrophes a transformer-based model and a conventional machine-learning baseline are taken into consideration. Some of the main performance indicators used to evaluate the models include accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. The problems caused by casual and distracting social media text are given specific attention. This project aims to (1) describe the challenges of collecting and evaluating noisy user-generated data and (2) empirically evaluate transformer-based text categorisation in a disaster-response setting. The research explores the use of AI-driven natural language processing on social media platforms connected to catastrophes to assist in the timely comprehension of crisis-related communication and human well-being. Moreover, it adds to the greater issue of Artificial Intelligence for social benefit.

items.abstract: Rapid urbanization, increasing motorization, and spatial concentration ofemployment and services are putting increasing pressure on urban road networks. Trafficcongestion is not only a transportation problem, but also a multidimensional urbanplanning problem that affects travel time, economic productivity, energy consumption,air quality, road safety, and social amenity. This paper explores the relationship betweenroad infrastructure and traffic congestion, identifies the main mechanisms that causerecurrent and non-recurrent congestion, and systematizes engineering, planning, policy,and digital interventions. A literature-based analytical approach is used, combiningclassical theories of demand, network balance, and bottleneck effects with recentevidence on demand management policies, intelligent transportation systems (ITS),artificial intelligence, and integrated urban mobility. The analysis shows that increasingroad capacity alone cannot guarantee sustainable reductions in congestion, as additionalcapacity may encourage additional car traffic. Road network improvements are morelikely to achieve sustainable results when combined with adaptive traffic signalmanagement, public transport prioritization, parking and demand management,coordinated land-use planning, real-time information, and multimodal accessibility. Aconceptual framework is proposed that considers road capacity, traffic demand, networktopology, control quality, and passenger behavior as interacting variables. The paperconcludes with recommendations for developing cities, which are particularly relevantfor the rapidly developing urban centers of Central Asia.

items.abstract: A smart city is defined as a city that employs communication and information technologies to enhance the entire process of governance, including making it more effective, public access to data, and enhancing the quality of government services alongside the well-being of citizens. Rapid population growth creates problems for cities associated with urban transport, air pollution, energy inefficiency, water scarcity, waste disposal issues, and burden on urban infrastructure. Smart city solutions include using new technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, Geographic Information System (GIS), 5G, and intelligent sensors, for efficient resource management. Smart city technologies help monitor different aspects in real time and make intelligent decisions in the areas of transport, health, energy supply, waste management, and public safety. In India, the Smart Cities Mission has made cities implement several technology-based initiatives for sustainable development and citizen engagement. In this research paper, the concept, design, technologies, applications, advantages, problems and perspectives of smart cities are examined, taking into account their applications in India.

items.abstract: Abstract The global community stands at a critical crossroads where technological advancement and environmental preservation must converge to ensure human well-being. This paper explores the multidisciplinary approach required to navigate global futures, focusing on the harmonization of economic science, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and digital innovation with sustainability metrics. Focusing specifically on the drought-prone Sangola Taluka of Solapur District, Maharashtra, this study examines how traditional agrarian economies can transition into sustainable models using precision farming. With over 73.96% of the workforce in Solapur engaged in agriculture, yet suffering from an average rainfall of less than 545-750 mm, integrating AI-driven resource frameworks is crucial. The paper provides factual insights into the pomegranate economy of Sangola and highlights how digital interventions can optimize water use, mitigate economic risks, and align local systems with Environmental Sustainability. Critical interventions such as IoT sensors, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for pathological tracking, and decentralized drone application systems are detailed to model an optimal input-to-output agricultural grid.

items.title: Technology and Communication in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Reimagining English for Global Futures
items.abstract: Abstract Technology has changed the way people use language and communicate with one another. The growth of the internet, smartphones, social media and artificial intelligence has brought major changes in the way we read, write, speak and share information. English, being widely used in education, business, science and international communication, has been greatly influenced by these changes. Today, communication is not limited to books, classrooms or face-to-face conversations. People communicate through emails, social media, video calls, online classes, digital presentations and AI-based tools. This paper examines the changing relationship between language, technology and communication, with special focus on English. It discusses how digital technology has influenced English language use and how artificial intelligence is becoming part of language learning and communication. The paper also looks at the advantages and problems of using AI in English education. AI tools can help learners improve their vocabulary, grammar, writing and communication skills. At the same time, too much dependence on such tools may affect independent thinking, creativity and originality. The paper argues that technology should support human communication rather than replace it. English education should therefore help learners develop language skills along with digital literacy, critical thinking, creativity and responsible use of technology. The paper concludes that preparing students for the future requires a balanced approach in which technology and human abilities work together.

items.title: The Dual-Edged Sword of Automation: Assessing the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Accelerating and Inhibiting Sustainable Development
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a fundamental catalyst for transformation across global societies, fundamentally altering the pathways available to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This paper presents a critical, socio-technical review of AI's dual role as both an enabler and an inhibitor of sustainability. Synthesizing recent macro-level consensus frameworks and empirical case studies, we demonstrate that while machine learning architectures optimize resource efficiency, power smart grids, and augment climate tracking, they simultaneously expose systemic vulnerabilities. These include severe ecological footprints driven by the energy-water nexus of hyperscale data centers, algorithmic bias that exacerbates socio-economic inequality, and a compounding interdisciplinary 'expertise gap.' This paper maps these dual-impact nodes across environmental, social, and economic dimensions, concluding with actionable governance strategies designed to guide policy toward a balanced digital-green transition.

items.title: The Economics and Operations of Lights-Out Manufacturing: A Comprehensive Analysis of Dark Factories in the Industry 4.0 Era
items.abstract: Abstract Industry 4.0 has brought about a paradigm shift of global production systems from traditional manufacturing to highly automated ecosystems. The pièce de résistance of this evolution is the "Dark Factory" or "Lights-Out Manufacturing", which refers to a production facility that is designed to run unattended with little to no human intervention throughout the entire process. This study investigates in the secondary data collected from industry reports, academic literature and corporate case studies contexts of dark factories technological framework, their economic potential and scalable operating aspects. Analysis uses data from 2013 to October 2025. Results indicate that fully dark factories remain a niche implementation limited mostly to high volume, high precision industries; however, "semi-dark" environments are being established based on the advances of Artificial intelligence (AI), Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and advanced robotics. The study comes to the conclusion that, continuous uninterrupted production and low variable overheads cost providing the massive economic benefits to the manufacturing industries. But at the same time the management must overcome the major challenges related to the cyber vulnerabilities, large initial investments and the socioeconomic effects of workforce relocation.

items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and conversational technologies are revolutionizing the tourism industry's digital interactions—shaping the way we connect with travelers globally.AI and conversational technologies have dramatically changed how the global tourism industry reaches travelers digitally. One of these innovations is the use of AI-powered chatbots by Online Travel Agencies (OTAs) to transform the way consumers engage with travel platforms, turning them into dynamic, personalized, and conversational spaces for booking. This research explores the role of AI-powered conversational agents in improving customer engagement and booking conversion rates within the highly competitive tourism industry worldwide. This research highlights the cognitive and psychological factors that contribute to user trust and satisfaction, such as the ability to provide 24/7 availability, custom itineraries, and smooth payment processing, in the case of generative and hybrid chatbots. Drawing from the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) paradigm and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the paper proposes that real-time algorithmic support to address travel anxiety and perceived value of the travel experience. Furthermore, it faces industry challenges such as AI hallucinations, data privacy, and the delicate balance between automation and the human touch. The insights provide actionable strategies for online travel agencies (OTAs) and hospitality marketers looking to adopt conversational AI, improve user journeys, and secure a lasting competitive advantage in the digital realm.

items.title: The Voice of AI: Consumer Psychology and the Strategic Use of AI-Generated Voices in Marketing
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence is transforming marketing communication, with AI-generated voices emerging as an increasingly important means through which brands communicate with consumers. This paper examines AI-generated voices from a consumer psychology perspective, focusing on how consumers interpret and respond to synthetic voices used in marketing communication. Drawing on literature from artificial intelligence, marketing, consumer behaviour and human–computer interaction, the paper explores the psychological significance of vocal characteristics such as naturalness, human-likeness, prosody, anthropomorphism and emotional expression. It further examines how these characteristics can shape consumer perceptions of message credibility, authenticity and brand trust. The discussion highlights the growing use of AI-generated voices across advertising, social media, voice commerce and interactive brand communication, with selected examples from the Indian marketing context illustrating their applications in personalisation, engagement and localisation. The paper argues that the effectiveness of AI-generated voices depends not simply on technological sophistication, but on how consumers psychologically interpret the voice and its relationship with the message and brand. The paper concludes by identifying directions for future research on AI-mediated brand communication.

items.title: Writing Parameters for 3D Printing of Dental Prostheses by Optimizing Them Using AI
items.abstract: Abstract We saw that the parameters for a dental printing process have a significant influence on the quality of the dental printed part, such as the layer height, speed of printing, orientation of printing, exposure time, and some parameters related to the used resin. There are many tra ditional ways of choosing the parameters, which are mostly empirical, and consequently lead to errors of dimensions, flaws on surfaces, and high consumption of material; there is also high production time. An Artificial Intelligence (AI) supported optimization scheme is proposed here for the optimal selection of 3D printing parameters to increase the quality and the production efficiency of individual dental prostheses. The proposed approach consists of data acquisition, data collection/preprocessing, feature analysis, training of the machine learning models, and optimization of the parameters to find out correlation between the printing conditions and quality factors such as dimensional accuracy, surface roughness, manufacturing time and con sumption of the materials. Various performance metrics are employed to analyze the different machine learning models and then the best one is utilized to determine the optimum parameter. There are plans to minimize the trial and error methods and to select the parameters on a data driven basis.

items.title: "Büyük Endüstriyel Kazaların Riskinin Azaltılmasında Tarihsel Evrim: BEKRA ve Seveso Direktifi Uyum Sürecinin Türkiye Açısından Analitik Değerlendirilmesi"
items.abstract: "Major industrial accidents constitute one of the most critical risk areas of modern industrial societies due to their high destructive effects despite their low probabilities of occurrence. Cases throughout history prove that these events arise not only from technical failures, but also from organizational weaknesses, systemic deficiencies, human factors, and inadequately designed safety systems. Root cause analyses reveal that the underlying causes of accidents are the insufficient analysis of reaction kinetics, the failure to correctly evaluate the accident chain developing after the loss of control, and, most importantly, the failure to keep risk analyses up to date. This situation proves that process safety should not be limited only to engineering design; it makes a holistic approach encompassing operational discipline, human factors, and organizational learning capacity necessary. The dioxin release that occurred in the town of Seveso, Italy, as a result of the uncontrolled shutdown of a reactor and the failure to correctly evaluate the by-products that could be released, fundamentally changed the European perspective on industrial safety and paved the way for the issuance of the first Seveso Directive. The Seveso Directives established within the European Union and the Regulation on the Prevention of Major Industrial Accidents and Mitigation of Their Effects (BEKRA Regulation), which entered into force in our country in line with these directives, constitute the fundamental legal and technical infrastructure for the prevention of accidents and minimization of their damages within the scope of technological disaster management. The Bhopal tragedy, which occurred despite the first directive being in force, and the Baia Mare accident, which resulted in environmental damage crossing national borders, became milestones in industrial safety and enabled the principle of “preventability of accidents” to be replaced by a more comprehensive understanding of “risk management.” In this process, critical requirements such as the domino effect, land-use planning, and informing the public were introduced into the directives. Lessons learned from experienced industrial accidents reveal that the “prescriptive” approach alone is not sufficient in the integration of safety management systems into processes. Current requirements make it necessary to adopt a “performance-based” approach that goes beyond the set of rules. Although significant progress has been made in our country in terms of regulatory compliance, there are still areas for improvement regarding process safety culture, organizational learning processes, and the internalization of advanced risk analysis techniques. For effective accident risk management, compliance with only regulatory parameters should not be considered sufficient; a performance-based, holistic, and sustainable process safety strategy should be ensured to permeate all operational processes. It is of critical importance that future studies strengthen interdisciplinary approaches and focus particularly on safety culture and organizational learning processes."

items.title: 200 Years of Children in Literature: On their Visibility, Value, and Agency
items.abstract: Across modern literary history, children have served as powerful symbolic figures through which societies negotiate core social values. Yet despite their prominence in canonical criticism, we lack a systematic account of how often children appear in novels, how they are valued, and what kinds of agency they are afforded over time. To address this gap, I conduct a large-scale computational analysis of 9,544 English-language novels published between 1800 and 2000. This study provides the first large-scale extraction of child characters from the modern novel, combining classical natural language processing with large language models to measure their visibility, emotional valuation, narrative agency, and independence from kinship structures. Contrary to dominant histories of childhood, children and adolescents become progressively less visible in the novel over time, a decline driven by the erosion of the adolescent girl in particular. Children maintain a more positive emotional valence than adults even as their agency lags behind adult peers, suggesting a broader portrait of children as sentimentally valued, yet structurally constrained social actors.
